image.alt: Ron faces Tar'Mo holding a curved blade to Elder Tiara, an elderly blonde woman in formal monastic robes, in Peak Temple's storeroom

paragraphs: 尋找眼睛，花了比龍恩想得還要更多時間。儘管有師兄塔爾莫的協助，兩人還是小心翼翼，以不驚動尖頂寺為前提的搜查。塔爾莫熟練於與人交際之道，龍恩的出拳則快狠準，能在對方意識到危險之前就將人擊昏，或甚至殺死。他們也有默契在短時間內先低調些，以免寺方注意到。這麼大的一間寺，少了幾個沒人在乎的小僧人，大概不會被發現吧？至少以龍恩過去的經驗，寺裡的道理大致如此。
有些時候，塔爾莫也會耍些小把戲，讓事情變得⋯⋯更有趣些。將僧人擊暈、確認後，再試圖洗清他的記憶，讓他迷迷糊糊地晃走；或是稍加蠱惑些，不過也無從問得多少有用的情報。在龍恩眼中，他不太懂為何要這樣做。一拳無法解決，那就兩拳啊？像這樣慢呼呼的，遲早會被發現吧？也太沒效率了？但塔爾莫始終提醒著他要有耐心，龍恩也就聳聳肩，算了。
「師兄，啊我們這樣再繼續找下去也沒進展，到底要等多久？」龍恩吃著乾糧，與塔爾莫在倉庫內休息。「在這樣熬下去，住持他們遲早會發現的吧？要不要直接來一發大的，一口氣搞定就好？」
「龍恩啊，你知道我們現在到底在幹嘛嗎？」塔爾莫露出耐人尋味的表情。龍恩搖搖頭。「我們是在製造恐慌。」
「恐慌能幹嘛？能幫我找到眼睛嗎？」龍恩不解。就只是找個眼睛，他不懂為何要把事情搞得這麼複雜？
「依照你的能力，尖頂寺就算知道你在這裡了，也什麼都做不到。」塔爾莫拍了拍龍恩的肩膀。「時間是站在我們這邊的，不用著急。」
「我還是不懂。那他們恐慌了，我們又能得到什麼好處？」
「小師弟啊，你知道尖頂寺有多少人嗎？」
「至少破千吧？但應該沒有兩千。」
「你的拳頭再快，要打敗兩千個習武之人，也得花上不少時間吧？而且打敗他們，和找到眼睛⋯⋯是兩回事。」塔爾莫意味深長的看著龍恩。「如果，他們自己幫我們把眼睛找出來呢？」
「什麼意思？」
「如果住持發現我們在找眼睛，他們一定會想辦法把這個眼睛善加保護的，對吧？你今天看見我放走的那幾個師兄弟，現在正幫我們看著住持他們在幹什麼呢！」塔爾莫微笑道。「再怎麼嚴加保護，整間尖頂寺要對抗你，都比不過。如果你拿到那顆眼睛，你能對抗的，甚至是這個世界，尖頂寺對你來說，跟螻蟻一樣藐小。」
「問題是我們不知道眼睛在哪。」龍恩點了點頭。
「沒錯，你想通了。住持那個性，肯定要開始有動作了。保持耐心，龍恩。保持耐心。」
住持的廳堂門口，傳來響亮的敲門聲。
「進來吧。」住持慢悠悠地說著，茶杯沒有放下。門被推開，三名僧人與一名格格不入的貴族女子，踏入了廳堂。「嗯？只有你們回來嗎？」
「師父，是小的錯。」尚恩雙膝跪地，向住持磕頭。「在我們護送休斯女士回尖頂寺的路上，發生了一些狀況。」
「果然，我的擔憂是正確的。說吧。」住持站了起身，向貴族女子輕輕點頭致意。「不好意思啊休斯女士，我想您也聽說了，小寺正在經歷一場格外令人頭疼的風暴，牽扯到您了，深感抱歉。」
「啊，不會的不會的。」蘿琳・休斯有樣學樣，向住持點頭致意。「這是我第一次來這裡，能親自接觸龍恩成長的地方，我覺得很有意思。啊，我是不是太冒失了，現在還提他的名字？」
「不不不，沒事的。」住持輕輕搖手。「請坐吧，至少我能為您倒一杯熱茶。尚恩，你說明一下發生什麼事吧，其他人可以先去休息。」語畢，尚恩以外的幾名同行僧人在向住持告辭後，便朝門口退去。
「是這樣的，師父。去程我們沒有遇到任何阻礙，在麥克嵩也一切順利，大概是我曾經在那邊參與比武大會---」
「講重點。」
「抱歉，師父。」尚恩挺直背脊。「我們和休斯女士說明來意，他知道是這等大事，幾乎沒有遲疑地就同意跟來了，而且事關龍恩，他也很願意協助。」
「謝謝您，休斯女士。」
「稱我為蘿琳就好，師父、師兄。」
「好的，真不好意思。」尚恩朝著蘿琳輕輕點頭。「回程時，依曼紐突然意圖對休斯女士非禮，然後他就、他就---」
「他突然倒下，就像窒息一樣，兩隻手抓緊他的脖子。」蘿琳邊說邊模仿當時的情境。「我也不知道為什麼，還想說他對我們在麥克嵩吃的食物過敏還是他有什麼疾病？」
尚恩點點頭。「結果沒想到巴多突然拿起他的棍子，站在依曼紐前面，威嚇著要把我們除掉，說是拉索斯的旨意。」
「拉索斯的旨意？」住持皺了皺眉頭。
「是的，那位師兄當時是這樣說的沒錯。」蘿琳點頭附和。「然後另一位弟兄就和他扭打起來了。」
「對的，史坦一看不對勁，就撲向巴多。巴多口中謾罵著各種不堪入目的話⋯⋯」
「『尖頂寺的走狗！』、『幫住持擦屁股的！』、『狗娘養的！』，呃，抱歉，我只是原話覆述而已。」蘿琳說完後摀住嘴，露出尷尬的表情。「我對尖頂寺以及住持充滿敬意。」
「沒事沒事。」住持揮了揮手，然後看向尚恩。「繼續。」
「我們想介入，但巴多壓制住了史坦，從口袋掏出一把奇異的匕首，架在史坦脖子前---」
「『你們要是想要把這婊子安全送回尖頂寺，就別阻止我！』然後他們就看著這名師兄把另一名師兄的脖子劃開耶！」蘿琳激動地在空中比劃。「喔對，他罵我婊子欸！」
「史坦死後，我們站在旁邊看著巴多用那把匕首將史坦的兩顆眼珠挖開，在手上把弄。」尚恩用手掌摀住自己閉上的雙眼。「然後他也對倒下的依曼紐做了一樣的事⋯⋯」
「他們知道了。」住持眨了眨眼。「他怎麼知道的？」
「這是什麼意思？為什麼他要這樣做？」蘿琳的眼神慌忙地在住持與尚恩間來回。「我的眼睛也會被挖出來嗎？」
「休斯女士，我想你可能還不知道龍恩想要什麼，以及他即將成為怎麼樣的怪物吧？」住持抬起頭，看向尚恩。「我們得加快行動了。」
冒險者們看向慌忙的瑪莉修女。他像第一次代班羅賓遜主教主持彌撒時那樣，不敢正眼看台下的任何一名信眾。
「當然，瑪莉。」薩梅爾輕輕微笑。「對吧，米多莉？」
「你已經是我們的一份子了。」米多莉對著瑪莉點了點頭。
「我是覺得都可以。」喜利抬頭看向瑪莉。「你想來的話，我們歡迎，但我們也不強迫你。」
「對啊，」波朝著瑪莉靠近了一點。「龍恩他⋯⋯似乎也蠻在乎你的。也許在這趟任務中，你比你自己想得還要更重要。而且，多一份力，算一份力。」波回頭看了看夥伴們，最後把目光停在 YHWH 的臉上。
YHWH 挑了挑眉，不多說話。對他來說，為師父茜卓博士復仇才是當務之急，誰一起來，從來都不是重點。
「那就當作大家都同意了。」米多莉看向法陣。「瑪莉，我們在這裡等你，你快去跟主教說吧！」
YHWH 終於開口。「也幫我們帶一點麵包來，我們也不知道會在那裡待多久。」
尖頂寺內的氛圍與前幾天截然不同。住持傳下的消息，另寺內的僧人們緊繃了起來。
按照住持的說法，近幾天，尖頂寺共有五名僧人遇害，三名失蹤，四名精神恍惚，看起來魂不附體。
眾長老已開啟閉門儀式，與住持一起在廳堂內誦經，加強前幾天以架起的魔法屏障。除非住持許可，否則任何人都不得未經允許進出廳堂。
走在廊道間，蘿琳還沒習慣尖頂寺如軍隊般的氛圍。這與他過往在麥克嵩的生活太不一樣了。
「那個，你們常常會這樣嗎？」蘿琳好奇地看著伴在一側的尚恩。
「沒有，這是非常極端的特殊狀況。」尚恩依然直挺挺的，每一步都踏地穩健。「我來到尖頂寺以來，這是第一次。」
「哇嗚，那我也是運氣不錯，能遇見這種『特殊狀況』。」蘿琳輕笑一聲。「對吧，師兄？」
「休斯女士，抱歉，這不是玩笑。」尚恩不苟言笑，但也盡量讓語氣輕柔了些。「我們都希望這段艱難的時期可以盡快結束。」
「好吧，師兄，恕我不敬。」語畢，蘿琳也模仿著尚恩挺直胸膛，擺出嚴肅的神情。「所以，接下來呢？」
「接下來我會帶你到女舍，讓其他師姐妹們保護你。」尚恩輕輕轉頭。「很抱歉，這種非常時期我們得這樣做。不然平常賓客來的時候，我們會安排個別住宿的。」
「哎呀，沒關係沒關係。」蘿琳搖搖手。「能體驗⋯⋯僧人的生活，也是很難得的。如果我講話太輕浮的話很不好意思，我還不太習慣這裡的氛圍。但，其實我想問的是，接下來尖頂寺會怎麼樣呢？」
「我們隨時等候師父的差遣。」尚恩望向遠方的眼神，讓蘿琳想起龍恩。以前有時候他搞不太懂龍恩在想什麼，現在他才意識到，可能單純是尖頂寺的人都有著這樣的眼神吧。
一名衣著不同的僧人躡手躡腳地踏入了龍恩的視線範圍。龍恩掄起手臂，蓄勢待發，但塔爾莫輕輕按住他的手。
「蒂雅菈長老是我們的人。」塔爾莫輕聲說道。他朝著接近的蒂雅娜長老點頭致意。蒂雅納長老回禮後，他便將長老拉進倉庫。
「巫妖大人，我們---」
「長老，龍恩還尚未成為巫妖，」塔爾莫看向蒂雅菈長老的模樣，就像他才是長老一樣。「稱呼他為龍恩就好。」
「啊，抱歉。」蒂雅菈長老尷尬的露出微笑。「我們正在閉門儀式，住持那傢伙讓我們每個小時一個人出來透透氣，我的時間有限。」
龍恩睜大眼睛。「喔喔喔，你是我小時候對我很嚴格的那個師姐。沒想到現在你變成長老了！」
「真是不好意思，要是我知道您即將成為巫妖大人，當時就不會這麼過份了。」
「長老，把握時間吧。」塔爾莫露出不耐煩的表情。「你不是才說你時間有限嗎？」
「是的是的，真不好意思。」蒂雅菈長老坐了下來。「住持知道龍恩在這裡了，也知道您正在尋找眼睛。但他現在能做的，就是閉門而已。把尖頂寺內外把關住，我想他也不知道該怎麼辦吧。」
「那⋯⋯你們知道眼睛在哪裡了嗎？」龍恩納悶道。「師兄說住持有可能會為了保護眼睛，刻意把它藏在哪裡。」
「這就是有趣的地方了。」蒂雅菈長老微笑道。「他也不知道眼睛在哪裡。」
「該死。」塔爾莫低聲咒罵。「這住持真是傻到不行。」
「但是別慌。」蒂雅菈長老看著龍恩。「你們住持想到了一個天大的主意。他有自信這能讓他找到眼睛在哪。」
「是什麼？」塔爾莫急切地抓住蒂雅菈長老的衣領。「說！」
「你也知道我無法說出口。」蒂雅菈露出遺憾的眼神。「住持對我們都下了咒。一旦說出口⋯⋯我們的命就沒了。」
「那樣的資訊，也是你對準巫妖大人最有價值的貢獻了吧。」塔爾莫迅速掏出彎刀，架住蒂雅菈長老的脖子。「龍恩，交給你決定了」

Finding the eye took longer than Ron had expected. Even with his senior Tar'Mo's help, they searched cautiously, taking care not to alert Peak Temple. Tar'Mo knew how to handle people; Ron's punches were swift, ruthless, and precise, knocking a man unconscious—or even killing him—before he knew he was in danger. They had also agreed to keep a low profile for a while, lest the temple take notice. In a monastery this large, surely no one would miss a few insignificant junior monks? In Ron's experience, at least, that was how things worked here.

Sometimes Tar'Mo played little tricks to make things... more interesting. He would knock a monk unconscious, check him, then try to wipe his memory and let him wander off in a daze; or he would charm someone a little, though it yielded hardly any useful information. Ron could not understand the point. If one punch did not solve it, why not two? At this sluggish pace, surely they would be discovered sooner or later. It was terribly inefficient. But Tar'Mo kept reminding him to be patient, and Ron could only shrug and let it go.

“Senior, we're getting nowhere searching like this. How much longer are we supposed to wait?” Ron ate his rations as he rested with Tar'Mo in the storeroom. “If we keep dragging this out, the abbot and the others will notice sooner or later, won't they? Why don't we do something big and get it over with?”
“Ron, do you know what we're actually doing?” Tar'Mo gave him an enigmatic look. Ron shook his head. “We're creating panic.”
“What good is panic? Will it help me find the eye?” Ron was puzzled. They were only looking for an eye. Why make everything so complicated?
“With your abilities, even if Peak Temple knows you're here, there's nothing they can do.” Tar'Mo patted Ron's shoulder. “Time is on our side. There's no hurry.”
“I still don't get it. What do we gain by making them panic?”
“Little brother, do you know how many people there are in Peak Temple?”
“Over a thousand, at least? Probably not two thousand.”

“No matter how fast your fists are, defeating two thousand trained fighters would still take quite a while, wouldn't it? And defeating them and finding the eye... are two different things.” Tar'Mo gave Ron a meaningful look. “What if they found the eye for us?”
“What do you mean?”

“If the abbot realizes we're looking for the eye, he'll do everything he can to keep it safe, won't he? Those brothers you saw me let go today are watching what the abbot and his people are doing for us right now!” Tar'Mo smiled. “However carefully they guard it, the whole of Peak Temple together is no match for you. Once you have that eye, you could take on the world itself. Peak Temple would be as insignificant as an ant.”
“The problem is, we don't know where the eye is.” Ron nodded.
“Exactly. Now you understand. Knowing the abbot, he must be about to make his move. Be patient, Ron. Be patient.”
A loud knock sounded at the door of the abbot's hall.

“Come in,” the abbot said unhurriedly, without putting down his teacup. The door opened, and three monks entered with a noblewoman who looked distinctly out of place. “Hm? Are you the only ones back?”
“Master, this is my fault.” Sean dropped to his knees and bowed his head to the floor. “Something happened while we were escorting Lady Hughes back to Peak Temple.”

“So my fears were justified. Tell me.” The abbot stood and inclined his head to the noblewoman. “My apologies, Lady Hughes. As you may have heard, our humble temple is weathering a particularly troublesome storm. I am deeply sorry to have drawn you into it.”

“Oh, not at all, not at all.” Roline Hughes copied his gesture with a nod of her own. “This is my first visit. It's fascinating to see the place where Ron grew up for myself. Oh—was that thoughtless of me, mentioning his name at a time like this?”

“No, no. It's quite all right.” The abbot waved a hand gently. “Please sit. At the very least, let me pour you some hot tea. Sean, explain what happened. The others may go and rest.” The accompanying monks other than Sean took their leave of the abbot and withdrew toward the door.
“Well, Master. We encountered no trouble on the way there, and everything went smoothly in Macksohn too. Perhaps because I'd competed in the tournament there—”
“Get to the point.”

“My apologies, Master.” Sean straightened his back. “We explained why we'd come. Once Lady Hughes understood how serious it was, she agreed to accompany us almost without hesitation. And since it concerned Ron, she was very willing to help.”
“Thank you, Lady Hughes.”
“Please, just call me Roline, Master, Brother.”
“Of course. My apologies.” Sean nodded to Roline. “On the journey back, Emmanuel suddenly tried to assault Lady Hughes, and then he—he—”

“He suddenly collapsed, as if he were suffocating, clutching his throat with both hands.” Roline acted out the scene as she spoke. “I had no idea why. I wondered whether he was allergic to something we'd eaten in Macksohn, or whether he had some sort of illness.”
Sean nodded. “Then Bar'Do suddenly picked up his staff, stood in front of Emmanuel, and threatened to kill us, saying it was the will of Laxthos.”
“The will of Laxthos?” The abbot frowned.
“Yes, that is exactly what that brother said.” Roline nodded in agreement. “Then another of the brothers started wrestling with him.”
“Yes. Stan saw something was wrong and threw himself at Bar'Do. Bar'Do kept shouting all manner of foul things...”

“‘Peak Temple's lapdogs!’ ‘Cleaning up the abbot's shit!’ ‘Sons of bitches!’ Um, sorry. I'm only repeating his exact words.” Roline covered her mouth, looking embarrassed. “I have the utmost respect for Peak Temple and the abbot.”
“It's all right, it's all right.” The abbot waved a hand, then turned to Sean. “Go on.”
“We tried to intervene, but Bar'Do pinned Stan down and drew a strange dagger from his pocket, holding it to Stan's throat—”

“‘If you want to get this bitch back to Peak Temple in one piece, stay out of my way!’ And then they just watched that brother slit the other brother's throat!” Roline gestured excitedly in the air. “Oh, and he called me a bitch!”

“After Stan died, we stood by and watched Bar'Do use that dagger to gouge out both of Stan's eyes and play with them in his hand.” Sean pressed his palms over his closed eyes. “Then he did the same to Emmanuel, who was still lying on the ground...”
“They know.” The abbot blinked. “How did he find out?”
“What does that mean? Why would he do that?” Roline's frightened gaze darted between the abbot and Sean. “Will my eyes be gouged out too?”
“Lady Hughes, I suspect you may not yet understand what Ron wants, or what kind of monster he is about to become.” The abbot raised his head and looked at Sean. “We must act faster.”
The adventurers looked at the flustered Sister Mari. Just as when she had first stood in for Bishop Robinson to lead Mass, she could not bring herself to meet the eyes of anyone before her.
“Of course, Mari.” Samael smiled gently. “Right, Midori?”
“You're already one of us.” Midori nodded to Mari.
“I'm fine either way.” Siri looked up at her. “You're welcome to come if you want, but there's no pressure.”

“Exactly.” Beau moved a little closer to Mari. “Ron... seems to care about you quite a bit too. Perhaps you'll be more important to this mission than you think. Besides, every extra pair of hands helps.” Beau glanced back at her companions, her gaze finally resting on YHWH's face.
YHWH raised an eyebrow and said nothing. For him, avenging his mentor, Dr. Chandra, was the urgent task. Who came along had never been the point.
“Then let's take that as everyone agreeing.” Midori looked toward the magic circle. “Mari, we'll wait here. Go and tell the bishop!”
YHWH finally spoke. “Bring us some bread too. We don't know how long we'll be there.”
The atmosphere in Peak Temple was utterly different from the previous few days. Word from the abbot had set the monks on edge.
According to the abbot, five monks had been killed in recent days, three were missing, and four were dazed, as though their souls had left their bodies.

The elders had begun the rite of seclusion, chanting with the abbot in the hall to strengthen the magical barrier erected a few days earlier. No one was permitted to enter or leave the hall without the abbot's approval.
Walking through the corridors, Roline still could not get used to the temple's military atmosphere. It was so unlike her life in Macksohn.
“Um, does this happen often?” Roline asked curiously, looking at Sean beside her.
“No. These are exceptionally extreme circumstances.” Sean remained perfectly upright, every step firm and steady. “This is the first time since I came to Peak Temple.”
“Wow. Then I suppose I'm lucky to witness these ‘exceptional circumstances.’” Roline gave a little laugh. “Wouldn't you say, Brother?”
“Lady Hughes, forgive me, but this is no joke.” Sean did not smile, though he tried to soften his tone. “We all hope this difficult time will end as soon as possible.”
“Very well, Brother. Forgive my disrespect.” Roline copied Sean, drawing herself up and putting on a solemn expression. “So, what happens next?”

“Next, I'll take you to the women's quarters, where the other sisters can protect you.” Sean turned his head slightly. “I'm sorry we must do this at a time like this. Normally, we would arrange private lodgings for a guest.”

“Oh, it's quite all right.” Roline waved a hand. “Getting to experience... a monk's life is a rare opportunity too. I'm sorry if I sound flippant. I'm still not used to the atmosphere here. But what I actually meant was, what happens to Peak Temple next?”

“We await our master's orders at all times.” The distant look in Sean's eyes reminded Roline of Ron. Sometimes she had never quite understood what Ron was thinking. Only now did it occur to her that perhaps everyone from Peak Temple simply had that look in their eyes.
A monk dressed differently from the others crept into Ron's field of vision. Ron raised his arm, ready to strike, but Tar'Mo gently pressed it down.
“Elder Tiara is one of us,” Tar'Mo said softly. He nodded to the approaching elder. After she returned the greeting, he pulled her into the storeroom.
“My lord lich, we—”
“Elder, Ron has not become a lich yet.” The way Tar'Mo looked at Elder Tiara made him seem like the elder himself. “Just call him Ron.”
“Ah, my apologies.” Elder Tiara gave an awkward smile. “We're in the middle of the rite of seclusion. That abbot lets one of us out for some air each hour. My time is limited.”
Ron's eyes widened. “Oh, oh! You're the senior sister who was really strict with me when I was little. I never thought you'd become an elder!”
“I'm terribly sorry. Had I known you were going to become our lord lich, I would never have treated you so harshly.”
“Elder, make the most of your time.” Tar'Mo looked impatient. “Didn't you just say it was limited?”

“Yes, yes. My apologies.” Elder Tiara sat down. “The abbot knows Ron is here, and he knows you're looking for the eye. But all he can do now is seal the place off. He's closed up Peak Temple inside and out. I doubt he knows what else to do.”
“So... do you know where the eye is?” Ron asked, puzzled. “My senior said the abbot might deliberately hide it somewhere to keep it safe.”
“That's the interesting part.” Elder Tiara smiled. “He doesn't know where the eye is either.”
“Damn it,” Tar'Mo cursed under his breath. “That abbot is an utter fool.”
“But don't panic.” Elder Tiara looked at Ron. “Your abbot has come up with a truly grand idea. He's confident it will let him find the eye.”
“What is it?” Tar'Mo seized Elder Tiara by the collar. “Tell us!”
“You know I can't say it.” Tiara looked regretful. “The abbot has placed a curse on all of us. If we speak of it... we lose our lives.”

“Surely that information is the most valuable contribution you could make to our future lord lich.” Tar'Mo swiftly drew a curved blade and held it to Elder Tiara's throat. “Ron, the decision is yours.”
